page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Above the text, centred, the running head "EPISTOLA". No margin notes, no footnotes, no page number, catchword or signature printed.

main_text.p: Illustrissima, debitor factus. Hinc munus, quod vides. Munus, fateor, perexile, si meam lucubrationem, tenuiculum; si tuum splendorem, qui non nisi splendida poscit; at magnum, si animum dantis gratum; at maximum, si rem ipsam spectabis. His accedit, quod his ipsis in libris Keckermannum, ma-gnum illum philosophiae quondam doctorem, afferere, & methodum ab illo traditam observare studui. Hujus viri scripta Anglis placere inde colligo, quod multa illius scripta ab illis sint typis descripta. Magnum hoc interpretor beneficium, quo τοῦ μακαρίτου scripta afficitis; & hac εὐσφωνήσει[?] gratias ago, non meis, sed discipulorum illius verbis, pro tanto, quo ipsius opera fovetis, favore. Accipe itaq; Illustrissima Academia, levidense hoc munus; exiguam hanc opellam ad judicii tui limam exige; eandem, ubi opus est, de novo refinge; scuto authoritatis tuae contra Theoninū livo-ris dentem defende; perexilem istam grati animi officiiq; mei significationem aequi boni consule, & juxta mecum statue, hanc beneficii esse naturam, redire ad eum unde venit.
Ad te redeunt, Mater Illustrissima, quae a te venerunt ad me beneficia. Ad me autem? Imo omneis Germaniae nostrae Theologos orthodoxos, qui scripta Perkinsi in pretio habent.
Profecto unius Perkinsi τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις[?] causa meam istam cuicuimodi est, opellam apud te symbolum animi mei ad praesens depono, & in futurum certissimi obsequii, prout debeo, pi-gnus,

page.notes: The Greek words τοῦ μακαρίτου, εὐσφωνήσει and τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις are small and tightly set; the accents and final letters are uncertain, so they are marked [?]. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. The word "Hujus" is kept with the printed j. The printed tilde over the u in "Theoninū" is rendered as a macron. The final line "gnus," is set right-aligned and continues the hyphenated "pi-" from the line before.
